ra: Mithras is the tutelary god of the Roman Mithraic mystery cult; wires the pre-existing Mithras into the new hub. Clauss ch.1.
Corax is the first of the seven grades of the Mithraic mysteries. Ostia grade-mosaic; Jerome Ep.107.
Nymphus is the second of the seven Mithraic grades. Clauss ch.10.
Miles is the third of the seven Mithraic grades. Tertullian De corona 15.
Leo is the fourth of the seven Mithraic grades. Porphyry De antro 15.
Perses is the fifth of the seven Mithraic grades. Clauss ch.10.
Heliodromus is the sixth of the seven Mithraic grades. Clauss ch.10.
Pater is the seventh and highest of the seven Mithraic grades. Clauss ch.10.
Cautes, the upward torchbearer, is a standing figure of the Mithraic cult. Clauss ch.9.
Cautopates, the downward torchbearer, is a standing figure of the Mithraic cult. Clauss ch.9.
The lion-headed time-god is part of Mithraic statuary, though its precise role is debated. Clauss ch.13.
The birth-giving rock is a core element of Mithraic cosmogonic imagery. Clauss ch.6.
The tauroctony is the central cult-scene of the Mithraic mysteries. Beck; Clauss ch.7.
Cautes and Cautopates are the paired dadophoroi (twin torchbearers) of Mithras, regularly flanking the tauroctony as a complementary pair. Clauss ch.9.
Cautes is an attendant torchbearer of Mithras within the cult scene. Clauss ch.9.
Cautopates is an attendant torchbearer of Mithras within the cult scene. Clauss ch.9.
Mithras is the petrogenes, born from the petra genetrix; the rock is the source of his cosmogonic birth. Clauss ch.6.
The tauroctony depicts Mithras himself slaying the bull; the scene is inseparable from the god. Beck.
The lion-headed Mithraic time-god is widely identified with Aion (and Zurvan), a god of eternity/unbounded time. Interpretatio is scholarly-attested but debated. Clauss ch.13.
The sixth grade, the Sun-Runner, is placed under Sol and embodies the cult's solar courier symbolism, linking the grade system to Sol Invictus. Clauss ch.10, ch.12.
